shots.name: Shooter Lane
shots.notes: Doubles as the right outlane — a one-way gate above the plunger lets drained balls leave without coming back into play. All three skill shots start here.

shots.name: Right Inlane
shots.notes: Cross this lane and an Orbit Multiball letter waits at the left loop for roughly five seconds.

shots.name: Left Inlane
shots.notes: The right loop is what this one lights, good for an Orbit Multiball letter. Because the inlanes light opposite sides, you alternate between them to spell ONE and TWO.

shots.name: Left Outlane
shots.notes: The only true outlane on the machine, since the right one shares a lane with the plunger.

shots.name: Arm Nukes Hole
shots.notes: Sitting just above the left inlane, this little hole feeds its ball back to the right flipper. Hitting it straight on from the right is nearly hopeless — bank the shot from the left, or hold the right flipper up and stab at it with the mini flipper.

shots.name: Bug Standups (Left)
shots.notes: Four targets side by side above the Arm Nukes hole — two yellow, one red, one green. Colour tells you which bug species you kill.

shots.name: Left Ramp (STARSHIP)
shots.notes: Advances your Recon Level and is lit for jackpots in regular Multiball. Slow shots roll back into the Orbit lock; very slow ones come straight down the middle.

shots.name: Left Loop
shots.notes: Runs all the way round the back to the right loop entrance. Unlit it feeds the bonus multiplier rollovers; lit it is caught by a magnet for an Orbit lock letter.

shots.name: Pop Bumpers
shots.notes: Three bumpers. Their exit lane runs just right of the left ramp, and that is where the ball comes back out. A Recon award's Super Pops raises each hit to 50K.

shots.name: B-U-G Rollovers
shots.notes: Three lanes above the bumpers. Completing B-U-G advances the bonus multiplier. A magnet just above the U drops unlit loop shots straight in here.

shots.name: Bug Standups (Centre)
shots.notes: Two green and two blue, flanking the bumper exit. Random bumper action hits some of them for free.

shots.name: Recon Scoop
shots.notes: Sits below the bumper area and collects your Recon award. Balls kicked out of the Orbit lock and the Warrior sinkhole are also served from here.

shots.name: The Warrior
shots.notes: A standup that walks backwards as you hit it. When one shot remains to light Multiball it rocks back and forth. It always spots whatever the sinkhole behind it is lit for.

shots.name: Warrior Sinkhole
shots.notes: Revealed once the Warrior has retreated far enough. Multiball starts here and Super Jackpots are collected here.

shots.name: Orbit Multiball Lock
shots.notes: A small sinkhole behind the Warrior, fed by a magnet that snatches lit loop shots out of the orbit.

shots.name: Brain Bug
shots.notes: Hides under the playfield and pops up in front of the right ramp and Recon scoop once a planet is cleared. It is enormous and almost impossible to miss.

shots.name: Right Ramp (TROOPERS)
shots.notes: The other half of the Recon Level ladder and the other Multiball jackpot. Slow shots drop into the bumpers.

shots.name: Right Loop
shots.notes: Mirrors the left loop. Lit by the left inlane for an Orbit letter; unlit it feeds the bonus rollovers.

shots.name: Bug Standups (Right)
shots.notes: Two yellow, one green and one red, just above the right slingshot. The easiest bugs to reach from a cradle.

shots.name: Right Mini Flipper
shots.notes: A small flipper above and right of the standard right one, on its own button below the main flipper button. Bug hits made with it count double.

shots.name: Left Flipper
shots.notes: Feeds the right ramp, right loop, the Warrior and the Recon scoop.

shots.name: Right Flipper
shots.notes: Feeds the left ramp and left loop. Holding it up and flicking the mini flipper is the practical route to the Arm Nukes hole.

goals.title: Rollover Skill Shot
goals.summary: A normal plunge ends with the ball parked on a magnet over the B-U-G rollovers. Exactly one rollover light is flashing: shift it under the ball with the flipper buttons before the magnet lets go, and you bank an extra bonus multiplier.

steps.action: Plunge without touching the flippers, then steer the flashing light
steps.detail: A normal plunge parks the ball on a magnet over the B-U-G rollovers — the magnet only works if you leave the left flipper button alone. Move the flashing light under the ball with the buttons while the magnet is still holding.

goals.title: Ramp Skill Shot
goals.summary: Plunge with the left flipper button held down and the catching magnet stays off, so the ball keeps running. Send it up the right ramp and you collect five million.

steps.action: Hold the left flipper and plunge full
steps.detail: Holding the button disables the magnet above the rollovers, so the ball keeps running straight up the ramp on the fly — five million, and it also nudges your Recon Level up.

goals.title: The Soft Plunge Lock
goals.summary: Not an official skill shot, but free progress. Hold the left flipper to kill the magnet, then plunge just hard enough for the ball to die in the Orbit Multiball sinkhole — that is one Orbit letter banked before you have flipped at anything.

steps.action: Hold the left flipper and plunge soft
steps.detail: You are aiming to run out of speed at exactly the right place, so it takes a few tries per machine.

steps.action: Let it settle in the sinkhole
steps.detail: Orbit Multiball needs six loop shots in total, so a free letter is worth chasing.

goals.title: The Bug War
goals.summary: The spine of the whole game. Six planets are attacked in a fixed order, each stocked with a different mix of four bug species, and you clear a planet by shooting flashing standups of the matching colour.
goals.reward: Progress through the planets, 100K-550K per bug
instructions: Colours map to species: yellow is a Warrior, green a Hopper, blue a Plasma Bug, red a Tanker. Shoot any flashing standup of that colour.
Antilles has 5 Warriors and 3 Hoppers. Zegema Beach has 4 Warriors and 7 Hoppers.
Dantana adds Plasma Bugs: 6 Warriors, 5 Hoppers, 3 Plasma. Tango Urilla adds Tankers: 8 Warriors, 6 Hoppers, 5 Tankers.
Planet P is the last stocked planet — 9 Warriors, 5 Plasma Bugs and 7 Tankers.
Bugs are worth more the further you get. A Warrior is 100K on Antilles and 300K on Planet P; a Tanker is 500K on Tango Urilla and 550K on Planet P.
The four displays above the flippers count how many of each species are left, and the number of lit standups shrinks as you clear them.
Bugs can only be killed in single-ball play, so a long multiball is time away from the war.

goals.title: Kill Bugs With The Mini Flipper
goals.summary: A standup hit with the right mini flipper counts as two kills instead of one. That halves the work of clearing a planet, and it is the single biggest habit change available on this machine.

steps.detail: It sits below the normal right flipper button and takes a while to stop feeling wrong.

steps.action: Take the right-hand bugs with it
steps.detail: These four sit right in the mini flipper's natural line.

steps.action: Flick it after a normal shot
steps.detail: Firing the mini flipper immediately after a hit made with a main flipper can talk the machine into scoring the double anyway.

goals.title: Capture The Brain Bug
goals.summary: Clear a planet and a huge target rises in front of the right ramp. Each hit is a million, and the number of hits needed grows every time — one, then two, then three. It is timed, and if the clock beats you the Brain Bug simply leaves.

steps.action: Bash it while it is up
steps.detail: It is a very large target, so accuracy is not the problem — the rebound is.

steps.action: Or cradle and let it escape
steps.detail: Whether you capture it or not, the next stage unlocks either way. Later captures cost so many hits that trapping the ball is often the better play.

goals.title: Advance Planet Or Arm The Nukes
goals.summary: Once the Brain Bug is gone, two shots light and stay lit until you use one: the Recon scoop advances you to the next planet, the Arm Nukes hole starts Planet Multiball. A hurry-up runs alongside, starting at 5M and falling to 1M, collected by either shot.

steps.detail: More planets flashing means a bigger Planet Multiball later. Advance unless you are already on Planet P, where the option is gone.
Starting Planet Multiball nukes every flashing planet at once — the fewer you have, the less it pays.

goals.title: Planet Multiball
goals.summary: The payoff for patience. Every flashing planet is nuked at once, and both the ball count and the values scale with how many you saved up: one planet is a 1M Nuke and a two-ball, five planets is a 12M Nuke, a 120M Super Nuke and four balls.

steps.action: Start it once several planets are flashing
steps.detail: Three planets pays 4M a Nuke and gives three balls; four pays 7M and gives four.
Left loop, left ramp, Recon scoop, right ramp and right loop each carry a Nuke lamp that goes solid once hit.

steps.action: Use the scoop for a Double Nuke
steps.detail: The Arm Nukes hole will also spot a Nuke for you and pay its jackpot.
Making all five lights it at the Warrior. Collect it and every Nuke shot relights for another pass.

goals.title: Regular Multiball
goals.summary: Walk the Warrior backwards to open the sinkhole behind it. Four hits the first time, six the second, and up from there. The multiball itself is four balls with both ramps lit for jackpots.

steps.detail: The Warrior swinging back and forth means one hit left to light Multiball.
Four balls, both ramps lit.
Jackpots start at 3M. Every unlit standup you hit adds to that up to a 4M ceiling, and lighting all of them awards an extra ball.
The Super Jackpot is 15M and stays lit for sixteen seconds; then the whole cycle repeats.

goals.title: Multiball Restart
goals.summary: If regular Multiball ends without you collecting a single jackpot, the machine gives you a second chance — roughly fifteen to twenty seconds to get the ball back into the Warrior sinkhole. The restart only serves two balls, but two is better than none.

steps.detail: The window is short and the Warrior will spot the shot for you if it is in the way.

goals.title: Orbit Multiball
goals.summary: Six loop shots in total, and that number never grows. Three lit loops spell ONE and lock a ball; three more spell TWO and start the multiball, with both loops paying 5M jackpots that stay lit throughout.

steps.detail: Left inlane lights the right loop and vice versa, for about five seconds.
A lit loop stays lit after you hit it, so three in a row down the same side is perfectly legal.

steps.action: Let the magnet do the locking
steps.detail: The third shot is snatched out of the orbit and dropped in the sinkhole.
Both loops stay lit for 5M. The first two loop shots each add a ball, up to four in play.

goals.title: Recon Awards
goals.summary: Ramps raise your Recon Level, the scoop cashes it. There are six levels and the awards get dramatically better as you climb — level one is a 1M bounty, level five hands out Multiballs and extra balls.

steps.detail: Each ramp shot moves you one Recon Level up. The scoop is lit for a level one award at the start of every ball.
Levels two and three bring Super Pops, Double Scoring, Spot Planet and Multiball Ready.
Four choices flash up and the machine picks one. Level four brings the Ramp Hurry-up and Nuke Chase; level five brings Multiball, Orbit Multiball and Extra Ball.

goals.title: Stop At Level Five
goals.summary: Level five is the sweet spot: it almost always gives you regular Multiball if you have not had one, and Orbit Multiball if you have. Level six mostly gives 25M — which sounds better than it is, because either multiball is worth far more than that.
goals.reward: A multiball instead of a flat 25M

steps.detail: Six levels, one per ramp shot, so know where you are before you go near the scoop.
A random Recon Boost can shove you up a level or several without warning, which is the real hazard here.

goals.title: The Recon Combo
goals.summary: There is a faster way up the ladder than one ramp at a time. Right ramp into left ramp into the Recon scoop is worth three extra levels on top of the ramps themselves.

steps.detail: The right ramp returns to a flipper you can shoot the left ramp with.
Do not break the sequence with a bumper visit.
The scoop closes the combo and pays the level jump.

goals.title: Psychic Test
goals.summary: The video mode, awarded from a Recon level one scoop. Flip through a deck with the left button and choose with the right. Match the machine's card exactly and you are given a Special; partial matches on colour or number still pay points.
goals.reward: Points, or a Special on a full match

steps.detail: It shares the level one pool with Ground Attack, Spot Species, Bonus Hold and the 1M bounty.
Left button cycles, right button selects. There is no shot to make and no way to drain, so take your time.

goals.title: Ground Attack And Air Attack
goals.summary: Two Recon awards that turn the bug standups into a slot machine. A two-ball multiball starts and the display flicks through values very fast — whatever it is showing when you hit a standup is what you are paid.

steps.detail: Ground Attack lives at Recon levels one and two; Air Attack is a level four award and pays more.

steps.action: Hit standups on the high numbers
steps.detail: The value cycles fast, so this rewards a fast trigger more than a clean shot.

goals.title: Klendathu
goals.summary: The end of the game. Nuke and clear all five stocked planets and Klendathu starts flashing — shoot the Recon scoop to begin. You get unlimited balls for thirty seconds, every bug standup lit, and a fifty million bonus if you finish the job.

steps.detail: Thirty seconds of unlimited balls. When the timer expires the mode carries on with whatever is still in play.
All the standups are lit at once, so flail — this is not the moment for careful aim.
Five million each, and the Double Nuke at the Recon scoop is ten.
All the bugs and all the shots pays fifty million.

goals.title: Raise Your Rank
goals.summary: The Arm Nukes hole quietly tracks how many times you have found it. Four shots makes you Squad Leader for five million, and a further run makes Corporal for ten. It is also the hardest hole on the machine to hit deliberately.

steps.detail: Cradle on the right flipper, hold it up, then flick the mini flipper. It works often enough to be worth doing.
Fifteen shots to an unlit Arm Nukes hole also lights an extra ball, so nothing here is wasted.

goals.title: Bonus Multiplier
goals.summary: Your end-of-ball bonus is built from the bugs you killed on that ball — roughly 100K a bug and 300K for a Brain Bug — and then multiplied. The multiplier comes from completing B-U-G in the rollover lanes above the bumpers.
goals.reward: Bonus multiplied by your B-U-G completions

steps.detail: Every completion is another multiplier. The skill shot gives you one before you have even flipped.
An unlit loop shot gets caught by the magnet above the U and dropped into the lanes.

goals.title: Where The Extra Balls Are
goals.summary: Starship Troopers hides several extra balls in places that are not signposted, and one of them rewards playing badly. Knowing all five routes is worth more than any single mode on the machine.
instructions: Fifteen shots to an unlit Arm Nukes hole lights an extra ball — a slow accumulation that is easy to forget you are making.
Fifty ramp shots lights one. The next threshold after that is a hundred ramps.
During regular Multiball, light every bug standup and you are awarded an extra ball on top of the jackpot boost.
Recon levels five and six both carry extra balls in their award pool.
Play badly enough and one is lit for you on ball three — a low score going into the last ball can be a gift.

goals.title: Ball Control With The Mini Flipper
goals.summary: Most players ignore the extra flipper for their first several games. It is not just a scoring shortcut — it is how you slow the machine down, drop-catching balls out of the Recon scoop and killing the speed of anything coming down the right inlane.

steps.detail: Scoop ejects come out fast; the mini flipper can catch them dead.
Take the pace off with the mini flipper, then catch the ball properly on the main right flipper.

achievements.title: Steady Hand
achievements.desc: Land the rollover skill shot for a free bonus multiplier.

achievements.title: Straight Up The Ramp
achievements.desc: Hold the left flipper on the plunge and take the 5M ramp skill shot.

achievements.title: Planet Cleared
achievements.desc: Wipe out every bug on a planet.

achievements.title: Brain Captured
achievements.desc: Take down the Brain Bug before it escapes.

achievements.title: Live Fire
achievements.desc: Walk the Warrior back and start regular Multiball.

achievements.title: Fifteen Million
achievements.desc: Collect five jackpots and take the Super Jackpot at the Warrior sinkhole.

achievements.title: Six Loops
achievements.desc: Spell ONE and TWO in the loops to start Orbit Multiball.

achievements.title: Recon Level Five
achievements.desc: Climb to Recon Level five and collect at the scoop.

achievements.title: Saved Them Up
achievements.desc: Start Planet Multiball with at least four planets flashing.

achievements.title: Squad Leader
achievements.desc: Find the Arm Nukes hole enough times to make rank.

achievements.title: Klendathu
achievements.desc: Nuke and clear all five planets, then start the attack on Klendathu.

achievements.title: Fifty Million
achievements.desc: Complete Klendathu — every bug and every Nuke shot.

drills.title: Three Plunges, One Button
drills.text: All three skill shots start at the same lane and the left flipper button is the switch between them. Leave it alone and the magnet holds the ball over the B-U-G rollovers so you can steer the flashing lane under it; hold it down and the magnet stays off, so a full plunge runs the right ramp and a soft one dies in the Orbit sinkhole for a free letter.

drills.title: Learn The Third Button
drills.text: The extra button below the right flipper takes a while to stop feeling wrong, so give it a whole ball. Drop-catch the Recon scoop kickout with it, bleed the speed off anything coming down the right inlane, and take the right-hand bug standups with it — a bug killed with the mini flipper counts twice.
drills.reps: one full ball using the mini flipper on every chance

drills.title: Bank The Nukes Hole
drills.text: The Arm Nukes hole is the hardest thing here to hit on purpose, and a straight shot at it from the right almost never lands. Bank it from the left instead, or cradle on the right flipper, hold it up and stab at the hole with the mini flipper — every visit counts toward rank and toward a lit extra ball.

drills.title: Ramp, Ramp, Scoop
drills.text: Right ramp into left ramp into the Recon scoop is worth three extra levels on top of the two the ramps give you anyway. The right ramp returns to the flipper that shoots the left one, so the string flows on its own as long as you do not break it with a trip through the bumpers.

drills.title: Count To Five, Not Six
drills.text: Alternate the ramps and count as you climb, because level five is where the multiballs live and level six mostly hands you a flat award worth less than either of them. Know exactly where you are before you go near the scoop — a random Recon Boost can shove you up a level without warning.
drills.reps: 3 collects, all taken at level five

drills.title: Take The Cross-Lit Loop
drills.text: Each inlane lights the loop on the opposite side for a few seconds only, so take the loop the return has already pointed you at rather than crossing the playfield for the other one. A lit loop stays lit after you hit it, which means three down the same side is perfectly legal — six in total, and that number never grows.
drills.reps: spell ONE and TWO in one ball

actionButton.how: There is a third button on the right side of this cabinet, but it works a flipper, not a game feature: it sits just below the normal right flipper button and fires the small flipper mounted above and right of the main one. Learn it anyway, because a bug standup hit with the mini flipper counts as two kills and it is the only sane route to the Arm Nukes hole.

howItPlays.objective: You fight the Bug War across a fixed run of planets, clearing each by shooting the flashing standups that match its bug colors. Climb the Recon ladder, bank the multiballs, and nuke every planet to reach the Klendathu wizard finale.
loop: Kill a planet's bugs by hitting flashing standups of the right color, and take the ones you can on the right mini flipper since those score as a double kill.
Clear a planet and the huge Brain Bug rises at the right ramp; bash it or let it flee, then pick the Recon scoop to move on a planet or the Arm Nukes hole to cash in a Planet Multiball.
Alternate the ramps to climb six Recon levels and collect at level five, where the reward is almost always a multiball rather than level six's flat award.
Empty and nuke all five stocked planets to set Klendathu flashing at the scoop, a finale of unlimited balls with a fifty-million bonus for clearing it.

lights.name: Bug Standups
lights.lit: Each standup's color names its bug species -- a Warrior is yellow, a Hopper green, a Plasma Bug blue, a Tanker red -- and a killed one darkens and knocks a notch off the species count above the flippers.
lights.flashing: Only a flashing standup is a live target on the planet you are attacking, and bugs die in single-ball play alone, so a long multiball is time stolen from the war.

control.effect: take standups on the small right-hand mini flipper, on its own button below the main one, so each hit lands as two kills instead of one

lights.then: Wipe out every bug a planet stocks to raise the Brain Bug in front of the right ramp. Clearing planets is the spine of the whole game, and the deeper you get the more each bug pays, from a hundred thousand up past half a million.

lights.name: Recon Level Ladder
lights.lit: Every ramp shot nudges you one step up a six-level Recon ladder, and the level you have reached holds until you cash it at the scoop, though a random Recon Boost can jump you up a rung or two without warning.
lights.then: Collect at level five, where the award is nearly always a fresh multiball -- regular if you have not had one, Orbit if you have -- and skip level six, whose flat twenty-five million is worth less than either. Right ramp into left ramp into the scoop jumps three extra levels at once.

lights.name: B-U-G Rollovers
lights.lit: A lit B-U-G rollover is a letter already banked, and each time you finish all three the end-of-ball bonus gains another multiplier.
lights.then: You mostly fill these without aiming, because a magnet just above the U snatches unlit loop shots and drops them straight into the lanes. Every B-U-G you finish multiplies the bug bonus built that ball.

lights.name: Orbit Multiball Locks
lights.lit: Rolling an inlane cross-lights the loop on the far side for about five seconds, and a loop stays lit once you hit it, so three down one side is fine.
lights.then: Three loops spell ONE and magnet-lock a ball at the sinkhole behind the Warrior; another three spell TWO to launch the multiball, and both loops then keep paying five-million jackpots. Six loops total, a count that never grows.

lights.name: The Warrior
lights.lit: Every hit walks the Warrior standup backwards, and the number of hits it demands climbs each time you do this, four on the first run and six on the next.
lights.flashing: The Warrior rocking back and forth is your sign that a single hit is left to open the sinkhole behind it.
lights.then: Start the four-ball multiball in the exposed hole and lift the jackpot toward four million by tagging the unlit center standups, then bank five and take the fifteen-million Super in that same hole. Lighting every center standup also awards an extra ball.

lights.name: Planet Nuke Choice
lights.lit: Once the Brain Bug is gone the Recon scoop and the Arm Nukes hole both light and hold until you spend one of them, while a hurry-up ticks down from five million to one beside them.
lights.then: Advance at the scoop to bank another flashing planet for a bigger payoff later, or start Planet Multiball now at the Arm Nukes hole to nuke every flashing planet at once -- five saved planets turn it into a twelve-million Nuke, a hundred-and-twenty-million Super Nuke and four balls. Make all five Nuke shots to light that Super Nuke at the Warrior.

scoring.text: Take a skill shot off the plunge -- leave the flippers alone and the ball settles on a magnet above the B-U-G lanes, where the buttons steer the flashing rollover under it for a free bonus multiplier, or hold the left flipper and plunge full to run the right ramp for five million. Then open the Bug War, killing standups on the mini flipper for double credit.

Climb the Recon ladder and cash it at level five for a multiball, spell ONE and TWO in the cross-lit loops for Orbit Multiball, and walk the Warrior back for the four-ball regular multiball. Clearing planets keeps raising what every bug is worth.

Empty every one of the five stocked planets with nukes and Klendathu opens at the Recon scoop -- thirty seconds of unlimited balls with every standup lit and fifty million for finishing the job. Banking planets for a full Planet Multiball is the other giant score on the machine.
